statements.status_notes: CVE-2011-3389 (BEAST) is the 2011 chosen-plaintext attack against CBC cipher suites in TLS 1.0 and earlier; it requires the client to negotiate TLS 1.0 CBC with an active man-in-the-middle injecting chosen plaintext, a browser-style scenario. The GnuTLS maintainer disputes the issue for GnuTLS and Debian has shipped no fix since 2011 (marked no-DSA); modern record-splitting mitigations and the deprecation of TLS 1.0 make the attack impractical. In this image libgnutls30t64 3.8.9-3+deb13u4 is present only as a transitive library dependency: verified in the built image, its sole consumer is librtmp.so.1 (curl's RTMPS protocol support; curl's own TLS engine is OpenSSL per `curl --version`), nothing else links libgnutls, and no shipped process terminates or initiates TLS 1.0 connections. There is no adversary-controllable path to a TLS 1.0 CBC session through this library.

CVE-2011-3389 is BEAST, the 2011 chosen-plaintext attack against CBC cipher suites in TLS 1.0. The issue is disputed by the GnuTLS maintainer and Debian has shipped no fix since 2011 (no fixed version exists). In this image libgnutls30 is dead weight: a DT_NEEDED scan of every ELF object in the built image finds exactly one consumer, librtmp.so.1, which is itself only reachable through libcurl's RTMP(S) protocol support, and no shipped component issues rtmp:// or rtmps:// transfers (zero rtmp scheme strings in the two libcurl consumers, librdkafka and the IBM DB2 clidriver GSKit library). Exploiting BEAST additionally requires an attacker who can inject adaptive chosen plaintext into a victim TLS 1.0 CBC session, a browser-style cross-origin oracle that a one-shot metadata-ingestion CLI does not provide.
